name: NativeWebRequestMetric
documentation:
Operational outcome of one native outbound {@link WebRequest}.

The normalized request target identifies the original logical request, not a later redirect destination. This value deliberately excludes URI user information, query strings, fragments, headers, bodies, and exception text. The original raw query is instead available as metric metadata under {@link WebRequest#queryMetricKey}. The path and query may contain application-specific information.

fields.name: attempts
fields.documentation: Number of HTTP attempts. Redirect hops within an attempt do not increment this value.

fields.name: cancelled
fields.documentation: Whether the caller cancelled the asynchronous result.

fields.name: errorCategory
fields.documentation: Safe failure category, or {@code null} when a response was received.

fields.name: hostname
fields.documentation: Lowercase hostname of the original request, or {@code null} when no valid HTTP(S) origin was available.

fields.name: method
fields.documentation: HTTP method of the logical request.

fields.name: nanosecondDuration
fields.documentation: Total elapsed time for the logical request, including redirects, retry delays, and retries.

fields.name: path
fields.documentation:
Raw path of the original request without query or fragment, using {@code /} when the URI has no path, or
 {@code null} when no valid HTTP(S) request target was available.

fields.name: port
fields.documentation:
Effective port of the original request, including {@code 80} for HTTP and {@code 443} for HTTPS when omitted,
 or {@code null} when no valid HTTP(S) origin was available.

fields.name: redirectRejected
fields.documentation: Whether a redirect was returned but not followed by the configured redirect policy or the JDK client.

fields.name: scheme
fields.documentation: Lowercase scheme of the original request, or {@code null} when no valid HTTP(S) origin was available.

fields.name: status
fields.documentation: Final HTTP status, or {@code null} if the request ended in a transport failure or cancellation.
